scope: Four local artwork repairs in the original muted stage. No base-background replacement.

prompts.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit target: the attached clean rendered paper-theatre scene. Return one complete, coherent wide landscape image at the same framing and approximately 1672 x 941 proportions. This is a careful local repair for an existing interactive website, not a redesign. Preserve object positions, the old muted dusty rose / sage / slate-blue palette, all paper textures, the background, the hills and bridge, the original paper dove and its envelope, the book, the basket and all large flowers.

Make ONLY these four repairs:
1. Small theatre canopy at image x 404–620, y 350–423. The short scalloped upper valance must be made of EXACTLY the same dusty rose/mauve matte floral-patterned paper as the long closed curtains directly below it. Remove its current orange peach highlights, golden sheen and satin look. Continue the same subtle floral damask scale, muted rose colour and paper grain onto the upper valance. Keep its existing curved top and softly scalloped bottom and its position beneath the arched frame. A soft narrow contact shadow should fall onto the long curtains below; the upper and lower fabric/paper should visibly belong to the same set.
2. The single pear standing on the floor left of the box at x 370–480, y 720–855. Redraw this whole pear as a naturally shaped small ripe pear, hand-painted with restrained watercolour and coloured-pencil stippling on matte paper. The pear has a gently asymmetrical rounded lower belly, a small natural base that sits on the floor, a smooth taper into a modest narrow neck, and one short curved brown stalk. Muted yellow-green skin with a subtle dusty reddish blush on one side. Smooth convincing pear silhouette and soft rounded shading. Absolutely no cracked skin, polygon facets, vein patterns, decorative marbling, zigzag lines, lumpy protruding bottom, bright shine or plastic surface. Keep its current size and floor location and the subtle contact shadow; surrounding fallen green leaves can remain.
3. The long stone staircase on the right. Keep exactly ONE continuous winding flight leading from the foreground to the distant city, same footprint, same perspective, no branching. Remove ALL raised parapets, railings, balustrades, curved coping rails, long raised side-curbs and vertical enclosing sidewalls from BOTH sides, especially the large curved wall around the left and foreground edge. Each step should have an open exposed tread and riser, and visible natural stepped edges with hills/foliage beyond. The foreground edge is simply the bottom step, not a high retaining wall. Do not replace the railing with a thin raised ribbon. Make the whole stair structurally coherent, treads evenly shrinking into distance. Keep the moth-embossed purple book and pink bookmark in precisely their current placement and scale.
4. The small closed hinged tarot box at x 550–840, y 670–855. Keep EXACTLY its current size, position, perspective, thin fitted lid and rectangular construction. Change ONLY the exterior surface decoration. Replace the pale grey striped wallpaper with a quietly coloured sage-green paper ground and airy, clearly readable trailing botanical sprigs: dusty rose wildflowers, sage and muted pale-cream leaves, fine warm neutral outlines. Restrained antique hand-painted textile-print character, harmonious with the surrounding rose flowers and green leaves, enough contrast for the box to look delicately decorative from a distance. No stripes, no muddied grey wash, no bright gold, no high saturation, no new emblem, no lettering. Pattern wraps coherently across the lid and both visible exterior walls. Keep the lid fully CLOSED and preserve every corner and edge.

Constraints: no annotations, no green or red marks, no text, no interface, no extra props, no new glow, no overall relighting, no global warm yellow or pink colour cast, no increase in brightness or saturation, no changes to any other scene elements. The result must keep the atmosphere and precise composition of this reference.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit the attached close-up of a pear on a paper-theatre floor. It is an exact local artwork repair.
The current pear looks wrong because its skin is covered in artificial marbled veins and its outline feels stiff. COMPLETELY REDRAW THE PEAR as a lovely natural small pear illustrated with fine softly layered gouache and coloured pencil on matte paper. Keep the pear at exactly the same position and approximate size in this crop.

An elegant real pear silhouette: plump rounded lower body, a gently narrower neck, a short slightly bent brown stalk entering a tiny depression at the top, subtle natural asymmetry, and one stable softly flattened base resting on the floor. Its skin should be SMOOTH muted pale sage-yellow-green, with a little soft dusty-rose blush on its right side and delicate tiny irregular brown speckles. Soft hand-painted volume, understated paper fibre texture, no bright highlights. Remove EVERY marbled, veined, cracked, geometric, floral or polygonal pattern from the pear skin. Do not carry the floor texture or background pattern onto the fruit. This should look like a quietly hand-painted actual pear, not a carved decorative object, a gourd, a faceted object or a photoreal sticker.

Keep the basket edge, dangling cloth fringe, the two pale olive leaves on the floor, floor colour and floor texture, shadows and crop framing in exactly the same places. Maintain the old muted dusty colour grade. A soft short contact shadow grounds the new pear. Match the reference's paper-theatre style. No new objects, no new leaf on the pear, no text, no borders. Return the same 49:36 landscape crop proportions.

prompts.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Image 1 is the EXACT clean image selected by the user. Image 2 only circles the area to refine. The user's drawn red boundary is a rough location guide, NOT a shape to trace.

Refine the compact stone staircase on the right into a beautifully resolved, structurally convincing winding stair. Keep its compact right-side footprint and keep its bottom at about y720, just beneath the book; do not spread it into the central stage or extend it toward the foreground. Redraw the staircase with a graceful, restrained S-curve and consistent perspective. The current stair has stiff abrupt turns, irregular pinches and an awkward snaking outline. Make the curve flow gently from the city entrance to the book. The two open edges should describe one smooth coherent flight, gradually widening from distant small steps to the near base. Every tread must connect to the next, with evenly progressing riser heights. At the bends, shape the individual treads naturally as subtle fans following the curve, rather than a zigzag stack of horizontal planks. Preserve a quiet handmade paper-cut illustration quality: slightly softened stone edges, fine neutral stone-paper texture, subtle contact shadows and believable depth. Keep the staircase supported by the layered hill; it must not float like a ribbon in the sky.
The lower footprint should be roughly 250 pixels wide around x1140–1400, with a simple low complete bottom step at y710–725. Upper path starts at the existing city entrance near x1315,y335. Keep the purple moth book and pink bookmark EXACTLY in their current place and scale, resting naturally on supported lower steps. No rails, no raised parapets, no continuous edging wall, no branching, no extra stair flights.

Also make the closed floral tarot box about 12 percent smaller overall, keeping its floor anchor around x692,y856. Scale its entire closed form uniformly, preserving its floral decoration, proportions, perspective and small contact shadow. Do not redesign the box pattern.

Preserve everything else in image 1, including old muted dusty rose, sage-green and slate-blue colours, paper grain, canopy, curtains, bird and envelope, pears and basket, bridge and flowers. No overall colour or brightness changes, no glow, no new objects, no text, no red marks. One complete wide scene with only these two refinements.

follow_up: Final staircase refines the rough marked footprint into coherent gently curved treads. Existing complete box is uniformly reduced from .85 to .75 about floor anchor (692,856), including its interaction area; generated box pixels are not used for scaling.
